criteria.live_only: Serve caret purely on demand: read_selection(node) reports the live selection record and set_selection(node, start, end, direction) replaces it, with snapshots carrying nothing caret-related. Caret-aware handlers add one explicit read; the snapshot record stays lean.
criteria.snapshot_only: Freeze caret into the dispatch snapshot as a nested selection record of start, end and direction, paired with a set_selection(node, start, end, direction) live writer and no live reader. Handlers read caret from the event they receive and write it back after normalization, the tightest surface that still closes the loop.
criteria.symmetric_calls: Freeze the nested selection record into snapshots while also shipping read_selection(node) together with set_selection(node, start, end, direction). Dispatch-time caret plus on-demand rereads support normalization, save-time sampling, focus repair and async resumption under one coherent reader/writer pair.

caret_projection.instructions: Select the caret and selection projection the Can browser boundary should implement.

criteria.flag_only: Expose only a composing boolean mirroring native isComposing on input and key snapshots, with the event vocabulary unchanged. Handlers postpone normalization while composing and detect composition boundaries from input-event sequences.
criteria.flag_plus_end: Expose the composing boolean on existing snapshots and add solely the compositionend kind, so handlers get both the running flag and a dedicated commit event while start and update remain unprojected.
criteria.new_kinds: Expose compositionstart, compositionupdate and compositionend as full event kinds, snapshotting the composing boolean and native event.data as a data string, with input snapshots retaining the flag for handlers that prefer polling it.

composition_signal.instructions: Choose how IME composition should surface to Can event handlers.

criteria.metadata_records: Project each chosen file as a record of name, size and mime inside change-event snapshots, mirrored by the read_files(node) live call, documenting that only the first 128 entries in selection order appear. File bytes stay off the boundary entirely.
criteria.names_only: Project chosen files as name strings alone, in snapshots and from read_files(node), with size and mime absent. Smallest shape, but upload flows cannot validate size or type up front.
criteria.opaque_handles: Project chosen files as opaque handle tokens in snapshots, dereferenced through read_file_metadata(handle) into name, size and mime. Handles bank a future upload capability no current workflow exercises.

file_projection.instructions: Select the file-input projection the Can browser boundary should implement.

criteria.chord_string: Project modifiers as one chord string per event, sorting held names as alt, ctrl, meta, shift and joining with '+' ('', 'ctrl', 'ctrl+shift'). A single terse field; testing one modifier means matching inside the string.
criteria.flat_bools: Project modifiers as four top-level booleans on the event: alt_key, ctrl_key, meta_key, shift_key. No fresh catalogue type is needed, though each snapshot grows by four fields.
criteria.nested_record: Project modifiers as a single nested modifiers record of alt, ctrl, meta and shift booleans. One added catalogue type, one added event field, and single-modifier tests read as direct nested field access.

modifier_shape.instructions: Select the modifier-key projection shape for browser event snapshots.

state.boundary: As of 27338b09, a Can browser event snapshot holds exactly kind, target, value and key, and nine kinds are recognized: click, dblclick, input, change, keydown, keyup, focus, blur, submit. Writes stop at attributes: setAttribute resets the default while dirty live input keeps what the user typed (probed), and checkbox change snapshots are indistinguishable between checked and unchecked, each reporting value 'on' (probed). Caret, modifiers, composition, multiselect and file choice have no projection, and live value or checked writers do not exist.
state.contract: R02 interface C-D frames each addition as a combined catalogue, checker and adapter slice exposing a bounded immutable projection: records frozen immutably at synchronous dispatch, live writers that accept explicit values, and caret or selection effects confined to explicit calls. Growth of the snapshot is additive alone, so the four current fields retain precise meaning. Returned collections are newly built copies that admit no mutable escape. View-scoped listener lifetimes and disposal rules persist unchanged. No external users exist, hence compatibility demands nothing further than the selected additive snapshot rule.
state.evidence: Proof combines native-DOM legs and emitted-Can legs across Chromium 140.0.7339.186, WebKit 26.0 and container-run Firefox 141.0, spanning dirty value and checked reset, autofill observation, per-field projection, no-mutable-escape behavior, and the unaltered legacy snapshot legs.
state.fixed: Decided already and excluded from this round: snapshot additions checked boolean and selected string array; live writers set_value, set_checked, set_selected; live readers read_value, read_checked, read_selected, read_files. Reserved for this round: caret treatment between snapshot and calls, file projection shape, modifier-key shape, and the composition channel.
state.workflows: The additions exist for these all-Can workflows: normalizing input while preserving caret; restoring dirty values and checked flags to defaults; noticing autofilled content; choosing, reading and resetting multiselect options; reading selected upload files; holding normalization during IME composition; mending focus and caret after rerender; range-selecting keyed-table rows with shift+click; reordering; independent disposal of views; and late replies that must leave newer edits intact.
